references.text: The parallel account in Mark, where four men carry the paralytic and dig a hole in the roof to lower him down before Jesus – the same event described with more details about the roof's construction.
The parallel account in Matthew regarding the healing of the paralytic, where Jesus sees their faith and forgives the paralytic's sins.
The immediate context: Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, and the Lord's power was present to heal. The men tried to carry the paralytic into Jesus' presence.
Continuation of the account: When Jesus saw their faith – the faith of those who lowered the paralytic through the roof – he said that his sins were forgiven.
The heroes of faith in Hebrews, who by faith accomplished great things – the men who lowered the paralytic through the roof showed perseverance and ingenuity driven by faith.
Jesus saw their faith – the faith of friends who went to the extreme step of breaking through the roof. This collective faith led to healing and forgiveness of sins.
The Mosaic law required a railing around the roof of houses, showing that roofs in Israel were flat and accessible – background for why the men could go up on the roof.
Peter went up on the roof to pray – this confirms the common practice of using the house roof, which is also the background for the action in Luke 5:19.
